body: Please add the error in text as well as in video/screenshot form (especially when it's obscured)

Please also include more system info in such reports, I suspect this is Wayland specific but the DisplayServer is not mentioned in the OP.

---

I tested and can reproduce the issue on KDE Wayland with Godot's Wayland display server (`prefer_wayland` editor setting).
It seems to be a regression as it doesn't happen in 4.6-dev4.

It doesn't happen with the X11 display server.

Error spam hints that it's likely related to Wayland embedding, CC @deralmas.

Hi, thank you for making me aware of this issue, let's see what's going on here.

Regarding the unexpected client-less event, it's not a critical error and in this case it might be a fluke, as `wl_callbacks` self-destruct after emitting their event. It's likely that there was a callback pending and, when the client disconnected, it was left orphaned (think of a signal without any nodes listening to it).

That said, I don't think that the embedder is strictly related to this, more likely the fact that there's some difference in behavior compared to other platforms.

The source of the error is this line:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/f5918a9d35350bf6402dd1b4902ab539747d77a6/editor/run/embedded_process.cpp#L419

It indeed passes a single argument, which it should not do. Removing that `false` argument should silence the error.

Now, why does it happen only on the Wayland backend? I'm not really sure. It's supposed to always refocus modal (exclusive) windows whenever the embedded game is focused. The relevant block of code is the following:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/f5918a9d35350bf6402dd1b4902ab539747d77a6/editor/run/embedded_process.cpp#L412-L421

Given that the call is invalid as-is, I think that either it happened on other plaftorms before and nobody noticed, or some condition (likely `!application_has_focus && focused_process_id == current_process_id`) never triggered there in the first place.

Update: I can replicate this on sway with _both_ the Wayland and X11 display driver (through XWayland). In the X11 case, I can reliably trigger it by hovering the game.

I also confirmed that removing the argument from the call silences the error, but I don't think that the logic should be kept as is, as it currently tries to grab the focus _continuously_, assuming that it will get it.

`grab_focus` maps to `DisplayServer::window_move_to_foreground`, which on Wayland is currently a no-op (I don't think we have APIs for that, maybe attention request?), while on XWayland it just turns the window red (as if it were an attention request).

I think that the original idea was to always force the focus away from the game to the modal window, but I don't think that it's a safe assumption to make for all platforms, especially X11/Wayland as there's a rich ecosystem of WMs and compositors, each with different focus behaviors.

Perhaps we could try "grabbing the focus" of the modal window only once per editor focus (i.e. only try every time you've freshly focused the editor) or maybe put `window_move_to_foreground` behind a DS feature flag. Not sure.

Aight, I made a PR, which should fix the issue. It looks like this is a regression from #110250. Classic find and replace, it happens :D

Regarding the above observations, it looks like X11 implements `window_move_to_foreground` with `_NET_ACTIVE_WINDOW`, for which there _is_ an equivalent in Wayland, our good old friend [`xdg-activation-v1`](https://wayland.app/protocols/xdg-activation-v1) (we already use it for attention requests). I guess I could hook it up for focus grabbing.

That said, my research stopped there. Personally, as a hunch, I still don't think that constantly grabbing focus is a good idea, since I don't _think_ that it's guaranteed, but the only way to be sure is to do more research on the matter.

> Please also include more system info in such reports, I suspect this is Wayland specific but the DisplayServer is not mentioned in the OP.

I omitted it because I thought it is system-agnostic.

I'm using X11 instead of Wayland.
